brief: Heading into September-quarter megacap tech earnings, UBS flags three investor focuses: core-business health, the path to AI monetization, and 2027 implications of the AI investment cycle for capex and free cash flow. UBS expects a strong Q3 season, citing record positive tech guidance and Nasdaq earnings growth above 50%, driven by semiconductors. Meta's ad growth (27% in 2Q, consensus 23% in Q3) is backed by AI-driven engagement, but FY26 capex of $130-145bn and deeply negative consensus FCF raise investor wariness. Microsoft's Azure growth (44% in June, guided ~45% for September) and Copilot's shift to seat-plus-consumption pricing support growth, even as FY27 capex is seen up 51% to $240bn and Azure margins have compressed to the low 50s. Google Cloud's 82% growth beat consensus and Gemini sentiment has improved, though free cash flow turned negative for the first time. AWS grew 37% with a record 39.4% margin and $496bn backlog, while 2026 capex guidance rose 66% to $220bn. Apple guided iPhone revenue growth down to 9-11% on supply constraints and memory-driven margin pressure. UBS sees depressed Chinese hyperscaler valuations as oversold against high-teens earnings growth, preferring Alibaba's inflection over range-bound Tencent, which holds upside if AI demand broadens into agents.
